title: Real-time electronic hand hygiene feedback on 16 hospital wards
subtitle: Cluster randomised trial with an outcome measured independently of the feedback system
statement: The hospital board intends to buy a real-time feedback licence for badge-based hand hygiene monitoring on all 16 wards on the strength of vendor claims. Whether feedback improves actual hand hygiene, rather than the badge system's own compliance figure, is unknown locally, and the obvious outcomes are biased: the system's figure can be gamed on feedback wards, visible observers change behaviour, and infections are too rare to compare in six months. A ward-randomised comparison with an outcome measured independently of the feedback system would answer the board's question.
whoAffected: Patients on 16 adult medical and surgical wards, the nurses, doctors and float staff who wear the badges, the infection prevention team, and the board deciding on the licence.
whatHurts: Poor hand hygiene spreads resistant organisms and C. difficile between patients. Buying feedback that changes the badge figure but not hand hygiene would cost money and staff goodwill, and alerts that feel like surveillance could damage trust in the monitoring agreement.
currentPractice: Silent badge monitoring on 16 wards with no feedback to staff; periodic visible observation rounds reporting 62 percent compliance; infection rates reported monthly.
whyNow: A board decision on the licence is due by June 2027, the badge system is already installed on all 16 wards, and 400 hours of independent observer time are available from January.
constraints: Six months from January to June 2027; 16 wards; 400 observer-hours; badge data at ward level only under agreement JSC-2026-07; no individual performance management.
patientCenteredGoal: Patients on every ward are cared for by staff who clean their hands at the moments that prevent transmission, whether or not anyone is watching.
summary: Problem framed as a ward-randomised comparison of real-time feedback with an outcome independent of the badge system.
